answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks through quadratic stake burning validated at the kernel level. To register N concurrent identities, an attacker must burn cryptographic stake scaling superlinearly as O(N^2) alongside verifiable work. Every node encrypts registration challenges with a time-delay cipher, ensuring old burn proofs cannot become a reusable relic to mint cheap agents. This makes large-scale identity spoofing mathematically cost-prohibitive.
